Myna
Live demo Numbers Gates Install Repository

16,926,848 parameters · 384d · 6 layers · 6 heads

It scans the state once, then answers without re-reading.

Myna is a gated linear-attention engine for typed choice, score and noul decisions over a growing observation: a fixed-size matrix state instead of a cache that grows with context, small enough to run on a laptop and export to a browser. It does not clear its accuracy gate. That is printed below rather than buried, at the precision the artifacts write.

The anti-prior experiment

A sampler flag meant to break label priors cost accuracy instead of gaining it: 0.4784612299508689 with the flag on against 0.5338735348381732 with it off — −0.0554 from the flag alone. The two runs print their own launch lines (SPEC §9.30), and these are the options they differ by: --anti-prior, --out, --resume, --steps — same --seed 0, same --batch 10, same suite and split, and both reaching 3,315 executed updates (last_step 3314 in each metrics file, the index one before the count). It is a clean negative, and it is why the next lever is data volume rather than a batcher trick. Sources runs/antiprior_on_s0c.report.json and runs/antiprior_off_s0.report.json, with the dose and the launch lines from runs/antiprior_on_s0c.metrics.json, runs/antiprior_off_s0.metrics.json, runs/antiprior_on_s0c.train.log and runs/antiprior_off_s0.train.log.

The witness line beside these arms is a scored competitor run in the same harness, committed in the same file: laya at 0.6668154761904762 (runs/antiprior_off_s0.report.json · macro.both.laya). It is printed because it is the denominator the gate was written against, not because this page benchmarks it.

The release gate, all seven rows

3 met, 3 not met, 1 open. Verdicts and conditions are imported from bench/gates.py, which checks each one against a committed witness under make gates — a gate cannot be greener than its artifact.

gatenameverdictcondition
G1 Accuracy beats the witness not met macro decision-v2 test ≥ 0.70 on the frozen split, per-source table published, ≥ +0.15 over the 0.4331 majority floor
G2 Latency claim survives equal-footing re-measurement met same box, same window, same question count, direct Agent call not Router; published ratio recomputed from that or withdrawn
G3 Deployment works for real met ONNX browser build answers a live page's decisions; bytes + p50 + cold-load measured in Chrome
G4 Long-context is correct, not just cheap not met needle-style typed decision ≥ 0.90 at 4k and ≥ 0.85 at 16k state
G5 Useful confidence, with abstention not met risk/coverage curve on calibration.jsonl; ≥ 0.95 accuracy at ≥ 60% coverage on banking77 + dbpedia14 + trec
G6 No regression on what already worked open synthetic v0 test ≥ 0.94
G7 Reproducibility met one command per result, seeds pinned, witness JSONs committed, pytest green

What the live demo demonstrates

https://myna-demo.onrender.com runs the 16,926,848-parameter checkpoint whose sha256 is 30f0fa937e57e8ce8b21c58315dc7e800151a0c95e003dc0930e0f75d588f1e5, at temperature 1.5. It shows two mechanisms; it does not show a model that passes G1.

  • Scan once, ask repeatedly. The engine observes the message once and every later question reads that same state — “scan a state once and ask” is the HTTP surface's own wording (src/myna/serve.py):
    • POST /v1/predict
    • POST /v1/sessions
    • POST /v1/sessions/{id}/append
    • POST /v1/sessions/{id}/ask
    • DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}
  • An abstention floor that prints n/a. --abstain-below withholds the commitment under the threshold, and with the floor off the engine returns no confidence and no margin rather than a fabricated one — return {"abstain": False, "confidence": None, "margin": None, "reason": None} (src/myna/engine.py:52). The demo renders that None as n/a instead of a number.

An abstention floor is a routing mechanism, not the product gate G5 describes: G5 is not met above, and no confidence on that page has been shown to predict correctness at the level the gate asks for.

Install and run it

Requires Python >=3.11. The wheel carries no weights — a pip install that silently fetched a training run would make every published macro a side effect of an install.

pip install myna-engine==0.1.0
myna-weights          # stdlib urllib: no gh, no token; verifies each digest GitHub publishes
myna-weights --check   # does the cache hash? exits 1 without writing anything
from myna import Myna, fetch_weights
myna = Myna(fetch_weights())          # test macro 0.5339, the best published arm
out = myna.predict("My order never arrived and I want a refund.", {
    "department": {"type": "choice",
                   "instructions": "Which team should handle this ticket?",
                   "criteria": ["billing", "technical", "shipping", "returns", "other"]}})
print(out["answers"]["department"]["choice"])   # → billing

Extras: [serve] for the HTTP API, [browser] for the ONNX export, [mlx] for Apple-silicon int8. Each published arm is a Release tag: antiprior_off_s0-weights is the 0.5339 control, antiprior_on_s0c-weights the 0.4785 one, v1b-checkpoint the 0.4893 Kaggle run.

What this is, and what it is not

  • Typed decisions — choice, score, noul — in one forward pass, not a generation.
  • Fixed-size state, so a longer observation costs the same as a shorter one.
  • Reproducible: 34 registry rows in bench/reproduce.py bind each published figure to one command and one committed witness.
  • Exportable: the browser artifact answers decisions in real Chrome with the probabilities the torch engine prints (G3 met).
  • Not G1: 0.4893271976084137 on the complete run against a 0.7 target, "pass": false in the artifact.
  • Not a trained-v1 product: the 0.5338735348381732 arm above ran 3,315 of 3,600 requested updates, and the harness that scored it prints that table as a VOID one (§7.1).
  • Not long-context-correct: G4 is not met — the state is cheap, the decision at distance is unmeasured.
  • Not useful confidence yet: G5 is not met.
  • No milliseconds on this page. The latency gate is a ratio; the numbers behind it are load-dependent on a shared box, so quoting them would be quoting the machine.

Reproduce every figure above

Each command re-derives one arm from the committed metrics file. They are the registry's own lines, printed from bench/reproduce.py.

uv run python -m myna.report --suite data/decision-v2-pilot --split test --metrics runs/antiprior_off_s0.metrics.json --laya runs/laya_decision_v2_test.json --out runs/antiprior_off_s0.report.json
uv run python -m myna.report --suite data/decision-v2-pilot --split test --metrics runs/antiprior_on_s0c.metrics.json --laya runs/laya_decision_v2_test.json --out runs/antiprior_on_s0c.report.json
uv run python -m myna.report --suite data/decision-v2-pilot --split test --metrics runs/v1b_kaggle_3600b.metrics.json --laya runs/laya_decision_v2_test.json --out runs/v1b_kaggle_3600b.report.json
make repro       # every published table cell against its witness
make gates       # the seven verdicts above against their artifacts
make secrets     # credential shapes in every blob reachable from a ref
make site-check  # this file is current and every literal on it re-derives
make site-mutate # the re-derivation can actually fail (page and artifact mutations)

And this page itself: uv run python bench/gen_site.py is its only writer; uv run python bench/site_witness.py re-reads the artifacts and refuses the file if any printed literal moved, and uv run python bench/mutation_site.py is the check on that check.

Figures as of 2026-10-02 — the newest commit among the run artifacts this page reads, so regenerating from that tree is byte-identical and the stamp does not move when the page is edited. Every number here is read out of a committed artifact or is arithmetic on two of them. Each arm prints its exact float; a four-decimal form appears only in prose beside it.
